text: Each app must know that it is really Aziz.

text: But nobody wants a face check every time they open an app.

text: So how can a bank know it is really Aziz, in every app, without checking his face every time?

text: This course builds the answer: heeyID, a customer identity platform that the bank runs inside its own walls.

text: Follow Aziz for one day, and the whole map appears.

text: Aziz installs the mobile bank.

text: It is the master app: it moves money, so only it may run MyID and TAF.

text: He types his phone number, and an SMS code arrives.

text: It comes through TAF, the state antifraud service of the mobile operators.

text: TAF checks that the code arrived on this phone, with this SIM card, and its verdict is green.

text: He types the code, then sets a password and types it a second time.
prefix: He types the code, then sets a password and types it a second time.

text: This one password opens every app of the bank.

text: Now Aziz has an account at level one.

text: The bank knows his phone, but it does not yet know the person.

text: In the marketplace, Aziz wants to buy a phone on credit.

text: The credit service needs level two: it must know the real person, with a real passport.

text: The marketplace is a side app, and it never checks a face, so it sends Aziz to the mobile bank.

text: There, the app first asks for his consent, and records it.

text: Then MyID, the national identity service, opens inside the mobile bank.

text: It checks his face and his passport against the state records.

text: The platform also checks his phone number against the numbers that MyID knows.
prefix: The platform also checks his phone number against the numbers that MyID knows.

text: Aziz is now at level two.

text: Next, the platform looks for Aziz in the bank's own customer records, by his personal identification number.

text: It finds him, and links the two.

text: His phone becomes a trusted device.

text: Back in the marketplace, Aziz taps Approve in the mobile bank, and the marketplace session gets level two too.

text: Each app gets its own access grant: this is Aziz, at level two, for this app only.

text: Next morning, Aziz opens the marketplace, then the mobile bank.
prefix: Next morning, Aziz opens the marketplace, then the mobile bank.

text: No face check.
prefix: No face check.

text: No new code.
prefix: No new code.

text: His sessions simply continue on his trusted phone.

text: One proofing serves every app of the bank.

text: Now the worry.

text: A stranger talks the mobile operator into moving Aziz's number to a new SIM card.
prefix: A stranger talks the mobile operator into moving Aziz's number to a new SIM card.

text: He puts it in a new phone, installs the mobile bank and tries to log in as Aziz.

text: He even guessed the password.

text: What stops him?

text: Not TAF alone: the SIM card really has Aziz's number, so the verdict can be green.

text: But it is a new phone, and Aziz was at level two, so the mobile bank asks for MyID on this phone.

text: The stranger's face is not Aziz's face.

text: At the same time, Aziz's trusted phone shows the login request, with two buttons: Approve, and This was not me.

text: Then the app asks him: does your SIM card still work?

text: It does not, so Aziz passes MyID again, the number leaves his account, and Aziz adds a new one.

text: Now look at the map behind that day.
prefix: Now look at the map behind that day.

text: The bank builds its own apps, and every app calls the heeyID API.
prefix: The bank builds its own apps, and every app calls the heeyID API.

text: Only the mobile bank holds the MyID and TAF SDKs.
prefix: Only the mobile bank holds the MyID and TAF SDKs.

text: The other apps are side apps: they use the password, then an approval in the mobile bank or an SMS code.
prefix: The other apps are side apps: they use the password, then an approval in the mobile bank or an SMS code.

text: Every request from the apps enters through one edge, and goes to the customer gateway.
prefix: Every request from the apps enters through one edge, and goes to the customer gateway.

text: All the rules of the bank live in that gateway: levels, limits, devices, sessions and consent.
prefix: All the rules of the bank live in that gateway: levels, limits, devices, sessions and consent.

text: Behind the gateway is Keycloak.
prefix: Behind the gateway is Keycloak.

text: It does one job: it issues the tokens for the access grant.
prefix: It does one job: it issues the tokens for the access grant.

text: Each app is one client, and each token names its app, so a marketplace token never opens the mobile bank.
prefix: Each app is one client, and each token names its app, so a marketplace token never opens the mobile bank.

text: The gateway never calls the outside world directly.
prefix: The gateway never calls the outside world directly.

text: It uses adapters: one each for TAF, MyID, the SMS service, the customer records and the push service.

text: In the mobile bank, TAF sends the codes.

text: The bank's SMS service sends them in the side apps, and in the mobile bank only when TAF is down.

text: Behind the gateway are four stores.

text: Postgres keeps the records.

text: Valkey keeps the counters and the cool-downs.

text: Kafka carries every event out, through an outbox.

text: Vault keeps the keys.
